channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: The Federal Reserve raises interest rates by a quarter percentage point
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years Wednesday.
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Alina Selyukh

item.title: Economist explains the Fed's decision to raise interest rates
item.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with economist Claudia Sahm about why the Federal Reserve chose to raise interest rates after months of keeping them steady.
item.content:encoded: NPR's A Martinez speaks with economist Claudia Sahm about why the Federal Reserve chose to raise interest rates after months of keeping them steady.

item.title: Trump's surgeon general pick faces questions on vaccines and vaping at Senate hearing
item.description: The Senate committee on health held a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third pick to be the nation's top doctor.

item.title: Head Start got her out of homelessness. Trump proposal threatens that help for others
item.description: A Trump administration proposal would change access to Head Start for children experiencing homelessness and the kind of care they would receive if they do get in.

item.title: Growing number of GOP candidates are using anti-Muslim rhetoric on the campaign trail
item.description: Anti-Muslim rhetoric has become increasingly common on the campaign trail at a moment when many Republicans are eager to shift attention away from the economy.

item.title: Federal budget cuts may force some states to end meal delivery for Medicaid patients
item.description: Some states deliver meals to Medicaid patients that address their dietary needs. Evidence shows it aids recovery and saves healthcare costs, but federal budget cuts may lead some states to cancel it.
